clue.text: Ineffective exhortation to inveterate consumer

definitions.meaning: doing no good, of no practical value
an urging to someone who habitually consumes too much: cut down your consumption, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the answer into USE LESS, the advice you would give a chronic overconsumer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ineffective is futile, achieving nothing of any worth.

clue.text: Someone unnamed and intrinsically average

indicators.note: within, so the word and goes inside the other piece

parts.note: so-so means middling, average
taken as written

explanation.surface: An anonymous person who is essentially ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intrinsically' means at its core, so the linking word sits at the heart of the average-meaning piece.
explanation.definitionFit: So-and-so is a placeholder for a person whose name is not given.

clue.text: Drop round to see one off

parts.note: a lap is a round of a track

indicators.note: one letter taken off the word see

explanation.surface: Pop round to see someone off on their journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one off' removes one E from SEE, leaving SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a decline or fall, as in a drop in standards.

clue.text: Rigorous dispute with Brown

parts.note: to spar is to argue
tan is a brown colour

explanation.surface: A tough argument with a former Prime Minister named Brown.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartan means austere and strict, like the discipline of ancient Sparta.

clue.text: One of two, level with each other

definitions.meaning: a single member of a pair found on the chest

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition splits the answer as A BREAST: humans have two.
explanation.definitionFit: Runners side by side are positioned alongside, neither ahead.

clue.text: Bally silly, old boy!

indicators.note: silly suggests nonsense, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An upper-class exclamation: how frightfully silly, old chap!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bally' is a dated British euphemism for 'bloody' as a mild swearword.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British intensifiers, bally being a softened form of the other.

clue.text: After time in the Bronx one can be worthy of respect

indicators.note: after places the second piece behind the first

parts.note: EST is Eastern Standard Time, used in New York
I'm able means I can

explanation.surface: A New Yorker's claim that anyone can earn respect with time.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bronx is in New York, which keeps EST; 'one can' said in the first person gives I'M ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Estimable means deserving esteem or admiration.

clue.text: Short tracks containing warbles about a little girl

indicators.note: the word for warbles holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: to warble is to sing

indicators.note: about means the girl's name is turned round

parts.note: Di is a short form of Diana

explanation.surface: Birds singing about a small girl along short railway lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the girl's name round to give ID; 'Short tracks' looks like brief songs, but they are railway sidings.
explanation.definitionFit: Sidings are short stretches of railway track off the main line.

clue.text: Early on I'm Norma, not a bad actress

definitions.text: Early on I'm Norma, not a bad actress

parts.words: Early on I'm Norma, not a bad actress
parts.note: a famous screen star speaking of her birth name, Norma Jeane, before she became a Hollywood icon

explanation.surface: A Hollywood star recalling her original name.
explanation.walkthrough: The star of Some Like It Hot was born Norma Jeane Mortenson.
explanation.definitionFit: The film star was christened Norma Jeane before taking her screen name.

clue.text: Scampering round army base

indicators.note: the word Scampering goes round, enclosing, the letters wanted

explanation.surface: Soldiers scampering around their base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' tells you the outer word surrounds the answer, which sits inside sCAMPering.
explanation.definitionFit: A camp is a military encampment where troops are based.

clue.text: Foul-smelling but safe aid to a curry

definitions.text: Foul-smelling but safe aid to a curry

indicators.note: foul signals the letters are fouled up, scrambled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pungent but harmless spice that helps a curry along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foul-smelling' does double duty in spirit only: 'Foul' signals the shuffle, and the whole clue describes the spice, pungent yet harmless and good in curries.
explanation.definitionFit: Asafoetida is a pungent resin used as a spice in Indian cooking.

clue.text: Approach plughole

parts.note: a plug is an advertisement, AD
a hole or opening is a vent

explanation.surface: Getting near to a sink's drain.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads one bathroom word, but it splits into 'plug' (to advertise) and 'hole'.
explanation.definitionFit: An advent is an arrival or coming, as in the approach of something.

clue.text: Wanted to have fashionable party in US, too

parts.note: in means in vogue
DEM is short for the Democratic Party in America
and means as well, too

explanation.surface: Someone sought after at a trendy American party as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wanted by many is sought after or popular.

clue.text: Outstandingly successful detective presents one with a bill

parts.note: golden, as in a golden era or golden boy
a private eye is a detective

explanation.surface: A star sleuth hands someone an invoice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' suggests money, but it is a beak: the goldeneye is a diving duck.
explanation.definitionFit: The goldeneye is a duck, and ducks are birds with bills.

clue.text: Threw up and expired, having secretly knocked back spirits

indicators.note: holding something hidden inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: died means expired

indicators.note: knocked back means the word is turned round

parts.note: grog is diluted rum, so grogs are spirits

explanation.surface: Someone who secretly downed spirits was sick and died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' makes SGORG; grog, naval rum and water, counts as a spirit, and 'having secretly' means holding it hidden inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To disgorge is to vomit or throw out.

clue.text: Regularly gobbles suet and fat

indicators.note: take every other letter of gobbles suet, starting from the second

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps eating suet puddings gets fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' takes the even letters of gOBbLeSsUeT.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means very overweight, extremely fat.

clue.text: Health clubs get Frenchman fit

parts.note: spas are health resorts or clubs
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur

explanation.surface: Gyms make a Frenchman physically fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' looks like healthy, but here it is a noun: a sudden seizure.
explanation.definitionFit: A fit is a sudden convulsion or attack, a muscular contraction.

clue.text: Pupae, cooked and thus consumed, make a hearty dish

indicators.note: consumed means eaten, taking the next piece inside
cooked suggests preparing, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: so means thus

explanation.surface: Pupae are cooked and eaten to make a filling meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' gives PEAUP from the larvae, and 'consumed' makes that hold SO; the definition is the soup itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Pea soup is a thick filling soup made with dried peas.

clue.text: Many in City chase rise during crisis

indicators.note: to chase is to follow, so this part comes after the rise

parts.note: to emerge is to rise up or come out
N stands for an indefinitely large number
Cy is a short form of city

explanation.surface: Crowds in the City pursue an upturn during a financial crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chase' means follow, so the city piece with N inside comes after the rise; Cy is a dictionary abbreviation of City.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency is a sudden dangerous situation, a crisis.

clue.text: Rival horticulturalists initially united to dig for food

indicators.note: the first letters of the three words

parts.note: a barb is a cutting remark, a dig

explanation.surface: Competing gardeners join forces to dig for veg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes R, H and U from the first three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb is a plant whose stalks are eaten as food.

clue.text: Against eating grub as an accompaniment to 18?

indicators.note: eating means taking the next piece inside

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
to grub is to rout, to dig up

explanation.surface: Opposing food that goes with soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 18 points to the pea soup clue; 'grub' as a verb means to dig, as a pig routs for roots.
explanation.definitionFit: Croutons are small fried bread cubes served with soup.

clue.text: Bill has thrown up stomach contents

indicators.note: in a down clue, thrown up means the word is turned upwards

parts.note: rennet is curdled milk from a calf's stomach

explanation.surface: A bill shows what someone vomited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' is money here: a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenner is a ten-pound note, a banknote or bill.

clue.text: An East European to be stifled by no French emperor!

indicators.note: being smothered by something means being enclosed by it

parts.note: non is French for no
taken as written
a Pole is from Poland

explanation.surface: A Polish man smothered by a French emperor's refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no French' is a single unit, the French word for no, which splits around the Polish man.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonaparte was crowned emperor of the French in 1804.

clue.text: Children, finally house-trained, remove footwear

indicators.note: trained suggests reshaping, so the letters are rearranged
the last letter of Children

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Once the children are house-trained, they take off their shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house-trained' looks like one word but splits: 'trained' rearranges N (from 'Children, finally') with HOUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To unshoe is to take the shoes off, especially a horse.

clue.text: Serene spirit comes from this

definitions.meaning: a distilling apparatus that produces whisky and other spirits

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is the apparatus used to make spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Still means calm and quiet, serene.

clue.text: Very ugly female novelist makes something to eat

parts.note: a gorgon is a hideous woman, from the snake-haired monsters of myth
Emile Zola was a French novelist

explanation.surface: A hideous woman writer cooks something.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorgonzola is an Italian blue cheese, a food.

clue.text: Interested in me? Sadly not

parts.note: I is the first person, me

indicators.note: sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rejected suitor asks if someone fancies them, and the answer is no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' makes NTO; 'Interested in' is the casual sense, as in being keen on jazz.
explanation.definitionFit: Being into something means being keen on or enthusiastic about it.

clue.text: Thin and angular, as Arachne became

definitions.meaning: in myth Arachne was turned into a spider, so she became spider-like

explanation.walkthrough: Arachne is both the setter and the Greek weaver transformed into a spider by Athena.
explanation.definitionFit: Spidery writing is thin and sharply angled, like spider legs.

clue.text: Gastropod consisting of muscle only

parts.note: abs, or an ab, is an abdominal muscle
alone means solely, only

explanation.surface: A snail made up solely of muscle.
explanation.definitionFit: The abalone is an edible sea snail, a marine mollusc.
